sources.fact: LBBD Planning Committee considered redevelopment of 14-34 London Road, Barking on 23 September 2025.
The proposal comprised 192 Use Class C3 units in a part 8/part 30-storey building.
The proposal also included flexible commercial floorspace including bar/event space, cycle/refuse storage, public realm, landscape, enabling works and basement.
593 notification letters produced four public representations, three of which objected.
Committee material treated the scheme as Build to Rent rather than conventional for-sale housing.
Committee discussion recorded 16.2% affordable housing and independent viability evidence that this represented the maximum viable provision at that stage.
Early and late review/clawback mechanisms were discussed so later viability uplift was not treated as fixed current affordable output.
The intermediate rent discussion referred to 80% discounted market rent initially and a deeper discount for two-bedroom units.
Conditions/S106 monitoring were intended to secure and monitor Build to Rent tenure covenants.
Officers recommended approval subject to conditions, a Section 106 agreement and any direction from the Mayor of London.
Committee resolved to delegate authority to grant planning permission on the stated conditions and Section 106 basis; this is a committee-stage resolution rather than proof of later final issue.

The committee resolution included a 23 March 2026 legal-agreement deadline with delegated ability to refuse or extend; this wave found no authoritative HTML readback proving what happened after that deadline.

examples.result: The 2025 committee proposal is fixed at 192 homes for this evidence wave.
192 is not added to an older Local Plan capacity because the current committee scheme is a separate planning-stage figure.
Committee resolution to delegate grant is not labelled final issued planning permission.
The Section 106 requirement is retained as a legal-agreement gate.
The March 2026 deadline is not converted into an assumption that the agreement completed or failed.
16.2% affordable housing is retained as committee-stage viability evidence, not guaranteed delivered tenure.
Build to Rent covenant monitoring is planning-obligation evidence, not HMLR title evidence.
Promotion remains zero until final current case status, exact title/site relation and statutory overlays are verified.
